messages:
alex: proposal: extract admission into a sandboxed policy engine (WASM) and keep the pool-operator focused on leases/placement/eviction. main wins: safe per-tenant rules, faster policy deploys, clearer boundaries. thoughts?
maya: neat idea. wasm brings op complexity but allows tenant-specific policies without rebuilding operator. my main worry is the hot-path latency.
jong: we can mitigate with a precompiled policy cache inside operator for hot lanes; fall back to remote policy server for cold paths. optimistic admit window still useful.
sophie: policy must return deterministic: decision + fallback model/quant + est_cost + est_latency + policy_version. versioning is key for audits.
ralph: ledger: central authoritative store for credits + local token-buckets for optimistic admits. policy engine reads cached ledger snapshots; invalidation should be push-based.
alex: rollout plan: simulation/advisory mode first (policy suggestions logged but not enforced), then gated enforcement on non-prod, then full roll. compare suggested_vs_actual.
maya: security: only signed/verified wasm modules allowed; require mTLS for policy server and attestation on engine boot. audit every decision.
jong: metrics to add: policy_eval_ms, cache_hit_ratio, deny_reasons_histogram, optimistic_mismatch_count. include trace_id in response for reconciliation.
sophie: operator should validate compatibility (region/gpu) after policy returns fallback; operator may override if SLOs would be violated.
ralph: i'll prototype a lightweight ledger read API optimized for policy reads and push invalidation websocket for caches.
alex: ack. i'll draft an RFC with API samples (WASM interface, admit request/response, failure diagrams).
infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-2210: "policy-engine admission prototype" and assigned to @alex
